questions.question: Distinguish between emotional appeal and rational appeal / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Emotional appeal targets the audience's feelings, using stories, music, and visuals to
  • evoke emotions like happiness, nostalgia, or fear, creating a personal connection with the
  • brand. By contrast, rational appeal focuses on logic, facts, and product features to persuade
  • consumers with practical benefits and evidence of value.

questions.question: How does advertising affect competition in the market? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Advertising can act as a barrier to market entry by creating strong brand loyalty for
  • established firms, making it harder for new entrants to gain traction. Conversely, it can also
  • be a tool for new firms to enter the market by creating awareness and demand for their unique
  • offerings. advertising fuels competition by shaping consumer perceptions, influencing market
  • entry, and affecting pricing strategies within industries
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Copywriting is a visual art too.' Comment. / [CO4]

questions.question: Define “umbrella branding” with an example. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Umbrella branding is a marketing strategy where a single brand name is used to market
  • multiple related products or product lines, leveraging the parent brand's reputation and trust
  • to gain market acceptance quickly. This strategy helps reduce marketing costs and build
  • strong brand recognition since new products benefit from the existing brand equity
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Define brand positioning in advertising. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Brand positioning is the process of establishing a unique identity and place for a brand in
  • the minds of the target customers. It differentiates the brand from competitors by defining
  • what makes it distinct and valuable. Effective brand positioning helps create strong brand
  • awareness, builds customer loyalty, and communicates the brand’s unique value proposition
  • clearly

questions.question: Discuss the advantages and potential challenges of advertising during prime time slots on television. / [CO2] [3x10 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Prime time slots command premium prices due to large viewership, making advertising
  • expensive for many businesses. With diverse viewing habits and streaming options, capturing
  • a unified large audience is harder, reducing effectiveness. Once prime time ad spots are
  • purchased, changes to creative or strategy are difficult to implement quickly.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Advertising can create false hopes and expectations.' Comment your views with examples. / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Advertising can create false hope and expectation by exaggerating product benefits or
  • making misleading claims, which can lead to consumer disappointment, loss of trust, and
  • negative brand reputation. Consumers feel misled by ads at times, and many report
  • dissatisfaction when products do not live up to advertised promises. While effective
  • advertising should be persuasive, it must also maintain honesty to avoid legal penalties and
  • preserve long-term consumer relationships. Consumers may suffer financial loss by buying
  • products that don't deliver promised benefits, and experience psychological harm such as
  • feelings of inadequacy or disappointment. False advertising damages consumer trust in
  • brands, making it difficult for companies to build long-term, meaningful relationships with
  • their audience.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the Diffusion of Innovations theory in detail / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Diffusion of innovation is a theory that explains how, why, and at what rate new ideas
  • and technology spread through a social system. Popularized by Everett Rogers in his 1962
  • book, the theory identifies five key elements: the innovation itself, communication channels,
  • time, the social system, and the process of adoption, which is often categorized into adopter
  • groups like innovators, early adopters, early majority, late majority, and laggards.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How do advertisements affect the purchasing decisions of rural versus urban populations? / [CO1] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Advertising affects rural and urban consumers differently, with urban consumers being
  • more influenced by factors like brand image and emotions, while rural consumers are more
  • heavily influenced by factors like product utility and are often more impacted by traditional
  • media like TV. In rural areas, local availability, cost, and recommendations from personal
  • networks often hold more sway than ads, while urban consumers are more receptive to
  • targeted ads based on personal interests.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
